# Fuel and engine {#sec-dd-fuel-engine}


::: {.cell}

:::


## Overview

DVSA and DVLA each record a vehicle's fuel and engine size, with different
labels and different gaps, and neither separates plug-in hybrids from other
hybrids. The pipeline checks the two against each other and against similar
vehicles, and builds one harmonised value of each. @sec-fuels-emissions
explains the fuel types and why they matter.

- **`fuel`** is the harmonised fuel, in DVSA's terms. It is the DVSA value,
  replaced by the DVLA value where DVSA says `Other` or the two clearly
  disagree, and checked against the fuel of other vehicles of the same make and
  model (methodology, [section 5.2](../../reports/methodology.md#fuel) and
  [section 5.3](../../reports/methodology.md#fuel-check-against-the-makemodel)).
  `fuel_src` says where it came from and `fuel_check` how it compares with the
  make and model.
- **`fuel_DFT`** is the fuel DfT's licensing statistics record for the
  vehicle's model, which unlike DVSA and DVLA separates plug-in hybrids. It
  is how plug-in hybrids are identified
  ([section 5.5](../../reports/methodology.md#plug-in-hybrids-the-dft-fuel-detail)).
- **`fuel_simple`** groups the harmonised fuel into six categories: Petrol,
  Diesel, Electric, Hybrid Electric, Plug-in Hybrid Electric and Other
  ([section 6.1](../../reports/methodology.md#derived-fields)). It is the
  column most analyses need.
- **`engine_cc`** is the engine size in cc: DVSA, else DVLA, else the most
  common for similar vehicles, and 0 for electric and fuel cell vehicles
  ([section 5.4](../../reports/methodology.md#engine-size)). `engine_cc_src`
  and `engine_check` record where it came from and what was corrected.
- **`fuel_DVSA`**, **`fuelType_DVLA`**, **`engineSize_DVSA`** and
  **`engineCapacity_DVLA`** are the values as supplied.

::: {.callout-important title="Plug-in hybrids are a lower bound"}
A vehicle is a plug-in hybrid in `fuel_simple` only when its DfT model is
clearly one. Models sold as both plug-in and ordinary hybrids stay as ordinary
hybrids, so plug-in hybrids are undercounted (@sec-pitfalls).
:::

## Coverage

The harmonised fuel is never blank: `fuel_DVSA` is supplied for every vehicle,
and 98.5% of harmonised
values are the DVSA value unchanged. A fuel of `Other` or a `fuel_check` of
`unknown_fuel` or `no_reference` means the fuel is not really known, or could
not be checked.

`fuel_DFT` is present for 94% of vehicles, those whose
model is found in the DfT statistics with a fuel of the same group. It is
lower for the oldest vehicles (90% of
those first used before 2000), as for the model match itself
(@sec-dd-make-model).

The engine size shows most clearly why the harmonised columns are worth using
(@fig-dd-fuel-engine). The DVSA engine size comes from the MOT history, so it
is missing for vehicles that have not yet been tested: only
1% of vehicles first used in 2024 have
one. The DVLA engine capacity fills most of these, but is itself missing for
older vehicles with no VES record. Combining them, and filling the rest from
similar vehicles, gives `engine_cc` for 99.1%
of vehicles, at every age.

## Values

How the values of each column change over time, by year of first use, from 1990. Numeric columns and
dates show the minimum, lower quartile (Q1), median, upper quartile (Q3) and
maximum; other columns show the share of vehicles with each value, with the
less common values grouped as *All other values* and missing values as
*Blank*.


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}

### `fuel`

Fuel type: DVSA; DVLA (same vehicle only, mapped to DVSA terms) where DVSA is 'Other', or says Electric/Fuel Cells for a DVLA vehicle with an engine; fuel of same-engine vehicles for an Electric/Fuel Cells vehicle with a recorded engine size; Electric where the make/model check corrects it. Never backfilled.


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![Share of vehicles by value of fuel, by year of first use.](fuel-engine_files/figure-html/fig-dd-v-fuel-1.png){#fig-dd-v-fuel fig-align='center' width=1050}
:::
:::


### `fuel_src`

Source of fuel: dvsa, dvla, variant (most common fuel of the same make/model/birth year/engine size), model (set to Electric by the make/model check) or dft (replaced by the DfT plug-in hybrid value).


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![Share of vehicles by value of fuel_src, by year of first use.](fuel-engine_files/figure-html/fig-dd-v-fuel-src-1.png){#fig-dd-v-fuel-src fig-align='center' width=1050}
:::
:::


### `fuel_check`

Fuel compared with the same make/model: ok, rare_conversion, rare_for_model, implausible_for_model, corrected_electric, unknown_fuel or no_reference (see methodology.md).


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![Share of vehicles by value of fuel_check, by year of first use.](fuel-engine_files/figure-html/fig-dd-v-fuel-check-1.png){#fig-dd-v-fuel-check fig-align='center' width=1050}
:::
:::


### `fuel_simple`

Fuel grouped as Petrol / Diesel / Electric / Hybrid Electric / Plug-in Hybrid Electric / Other.


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![Share of vehicles by value of fuel_simple, by year of first use.](fuel-engine_files/figure-html/fig-dd-v-fuel-simple-1.png){#fig-dd-v-fuel-simple fig-align='center' width=1050}
:::
:::


### `fuel_DFT`

Fuel as the DfT vehicle licensing statistics record it for this make and model (VEH0220), which unlike DVSA and DVLA separates plug-in hybrids from other hybrids. NA where the make/model has no DfT vehicles of this fuel group, or where no one DfT fuel is common enough to choose (see fuel_DFT_src).


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![Share of vehicles by value of fuel_DFT, by year of first use.](fuel-engine_files/figure-html/fig-dd-v-fuel-dft-1.png){#fig-dd-v-fuel-dft fig-align='center' width=1050}
:::
:::


### `fuel_DFT_src`

How fuel_DFT was found: dft_model (the DfT model string's most common fuel of this group), dft_genmodel (the generic model's), ambiguous_model / ambiguous_genmodel (a match, but no single DfT fuel reaches the checks.dft_fuel_share threshold) or no_reference.
